newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Resources buoy Australian stocks at open.
newsitem.headline: Resources buoy Australian stocks at open.

text.p: Australian shares started on a firmer note on Tuesday with investors snapping up key resource issues after base metal prices rose on Monday and after the Dow broke a three session losing streak.
At 10.15 a.m. (2315 GMT), the All Ordinaries index was 9.5 points higher at 2,430.7.
The March share price index was up 26 points at 2,419 and at an 11.7 point discount to the underlying index.
Australia's largest company, the Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd found the most buying attention early, while CRA Ltd also found backing.
"The market got off to a good start but support for some of the banks dried up fairly quickly," a dealer at a Sydney-based brokerage said.

The dealer said the lack of support for the bank sector underscored the main concern of investors -- that a possible interest rate rise in the U.S. could take the shine off the local bond market, making the high-yielding bank issues look less attractive.

"It's a hard market to call at the moment. Volume has been thin so far and I think a lot of players are waiting to see the outcome of (January) retail trade data due out later this morning," the dealer said.
